title: soc2-prep-scratchpad-elliot-brooks
content:
SOC2 prep scratchpad - Elliot

Goal: quick capture of open questions, evidence locations, and todo owners while we iterate the control mapping doc. This is messy - intended to be ephemeral.

High-level status:
- Overall readiness: mid-stage. Most policies exist, need tighter evidence bundles and some automation for evidence collection (esp change mgmt + backups).
- Audit kickoff planned: 2025-02-01 (tentative). Need final control mapping 2 weeks prior.

Open questions / unknowns:
1) Logical access (CC6): do we have a single exported report showing active user lists + MFA status across cloud console + SSO?
   - Current: Okta export exists (okta-admin-exports/2024-10/active-users.csv), but need cross-check with GCP and AWS console users.
   - TODO: @Maya to run cross-account user reconciliation script (JIRA:INFRA-210).
2) Change management (CC7): can we produce a 6-month filtered view of code deployments with approvals (PR + CI) tied to releases?
   - Partial: GitHub PR history + CI logs available; approvals not always enforced for infra repo.
   - Decision pending: enforce branch protection on infra repos. @Priya to draft enforcement plan.
3) Backups & restore evidence: where are retention policies captured? snapshots vs DB exports?
   - Evidence we need: regular backup schedule, restore test logs, retention policy doc.
   - Stored in: shared_drives/security-and-compliance/backups/ and shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/backups-2024/

Control -> Evidence rough mapping (working):
- CC6 (Logical Access): Okta export, SSO config screenshot, access review emails (quarterly-access-review-2024.pdf)
- CC7 (Change Mgmt): GitHub PRs (codeowner approvals), CI run logs (ci-logs/), JIRA tickets with approval labels (SEC-321 examples)
- CC8 (System Ops & Availability): SRE runbooks (sre/runbooks/), monitoring alerts + incident postmortems (pagerduty-export-2024-09.csv)
- CC9 (Backups): DB snapshot schedule screenshots, restore-test-2024-10-12.log

Evidence collection notes:
- Prefer single zip per control with README listing files and query used to generate (helps auditor).
- Name convention: soc2-evidence/<control>-<YYYYMMDD>-<owner>.zip

Immediate TODOs (this doc):
- [ ] @Maya: run Okta <> cloud user reconciliation (due 2024-11-14) - link INFRA-210
- [ ] @Priya: draft branch protection + enforcement proposal for infra repos (due 2024-11-21)
- [ ] @Ryan: collect restore test logs and move to shared_drives/security-and-compliance/backups/ (due 2024-11-18)
- [ ] Elliot: assemble initial control zip bundles and upload to shared_drives/security-and-compliance/audit-evidence/drafts/ (due 2024-11-22)

Quick notes / brain dump:
- Might ask infra to enable a nightly job that exports active IAM bindings across GCP projects into a central bucket - eases evidence pulls.
- Consider lightweight automation: small Lambda/GCF that zips evidence per control on demand. Low priority but big time-saver.
- Watch out for PII in evidence bundles - redact or provide gated links.

Questions for lead auditor (to ask in kickoff):
- Preferred evidence format? (single PDF per control vs zipped raw artifacts)
- Do they accept screenshots + query reproductions?

Links / refs:
- Confluence: SOC2-Readiness (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/SOC2-Readiness)
- Example evidence naming: shared_drives/security-and-compliance/examples/soc2-evidence-sample.zip
- Slack channel: #soc2-prep (thread: t1234567890)

Last quick thought: keep this doc focused on the minimal set to satisfy in-scope SOC2 controls. Anything nice-to-have can be moved to a separate "audit-improvements" backlog after baseline is shipped.

-- Elliot
